skill.name: ddd-strategic-design
skill.description: Plan DDD strategic design artifacts for complex business domains, including subdomains, bounded contexts, and ubiquitous language.
skill.summary: Create DDD strategic design artifacts for domain boundaries, ownership, and shared language.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Both static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks in prose and a fenced text example. I found no executable code, command execution intent, prompt injection attempt, or data exfiltration behavior in the reviewed skill files.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 31 uses Markdown inline backticks around references/strategic-design-template.md as a file name. It is prose guidance to open a template, not Ruby or shell command execution.

content.value_statement: Complex domains often hide unclear ownership and mixed business language. This skill guides Codex, Claude, and Claude Code through subdomain classification, bounded contexts, and shared terminology.
actual_capabilities: Extracts domain capabilities and classifies them as core, supporting, or generic subdomains.
Defines bounded contexts around consistency needs, responsibilities, dependencies, and ownership.
Builds a ubiquitous language glossary with canonical terms and context-specific meanings.
Captures boundary decisions and rationale for architecture decision records.
Uses a strategic design template for subdomain tables, context catalogs, and glossary entries.
limitations: It does not generate executable application code.
It needs stakeholder input to validate business truth.
It does not replace tactical DDD modeling after boundaries are chosen.
It is not intended for infrastructure-only or UI-only tasks.

use_cases.title: Map a New Business Domain
use_cases.description: Identify capabilities, classify subdomains, and name early bounded contexts before teams start implementation.

use_cases.title: Split a Large Monolith
use_cases.description: Review responsibilities and dependencies to propose domain boundaries for a modernization effort.

use_cases.title: Align Team Ownership
use_cases.description: Connect bounded contexts to owner teams and document the rationale for future delivery planning.

prompt_templates.title: Classify Subdomains
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis for a known domain
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to list our main business capabilities, classify each subdomain, and explain the reason for each classification.

prompt_templates.title: Define Bounded Contexts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to turn these capabilities into bounded contexts with responsibilities, upstream dependencies, downstream consumers, and owner teams.

prompt_templates.title: Create Shared Language
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate glossary work with domain experts
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to build a ubiquitous language glossary for this domain, including terms, definitions, contexts, and terms we should avoid.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Boundary ADRs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to evaluate these boundary options and draft ADR-ready decisions with context, tradeoffs, ownership, and implementation impact.

output_examples.input: Map a commerce domain with catalog, pricing, checkout, fulfillment, billing, and identity capabilities.
output: Subdomain classification separates pricing as core, identity as supporting, and billing as supporting.
Bounded context catalog defines Catalog, Checkout, Fulfillment, and Billing responsibilities.
Ownership notes connect Commerce, Platform, and Finance teams to the proposed contexts.

output_examples.input: Create a shared language for order placement and inventory reservation.
output: Glossary defines Order as a confirmed purchase request in Checkout.
Glossary defines Reservation as a temporary inventory hold in Fulfillment.
Anti-terms flag vague words that mean different things across teams.

output_examples.input: Assess whether checkout and payment should be one context or separate contexts.
output: Boundary decision compares consistency needs, ownership, compliance concerns, and consumer dependencies.
Recommendation documents the chosen boundary and the reason for the decision.
Follow-up notes identify tactical modeling work needed before implementation.

best_practices: Bring concrete business workflows and stakeholder language before asking for boundary recommendations.
Validate classifications with domain experts before using them for team structure or delivery planning.
Record boundary decisions with rationale so future teams understand the tradeoffs.
anti_patterns: Do not use technical layers as bounded contexts without checking business ownership.
Do not classify every important capability as core without a differentiation reason.
Do not treat the first glossary as final without stakeholder review.

faq.question: What is this skill for?
faq.answer: It helps design DDD strategic artifacts such as subdomain classifications, bounded contexts, and ubiquitous language.

faq.question: Does it write production code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on domain boundaries, ownership, language, and decision records before implementation.

faq.question: Can it split a monolith?
faq.answer: It can propose domain boundaries and migration-oriented context candidates from business capabilities and dependencies.

faq.question: What input works best?
faq.answer: Provide business workflows, teams, systems, terms, pain points, and known dependencies.

faq.question: Does it need domain experts?
faq.answer: Yes. The output should be reviewed with domain experts because the skill cannot verify business truth alone.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
